integration_findings.severity: blocks every mode with a strict trainer at the initial LoRA sync
integration_findings.what:
runtime/megatron_lora.lora_sha256 (key
 + shape
 + bytes) is not muse_glimmer_lora_sha256_v1 (name|dtype|shape
 + bytes) of e2e/sync.py; StrictTrainer.export_lora reports the former, export_lora_verified / RemoteTrainer recompute the latter and fail closed (WeightSyncError).
integration_findings.patch: runtime/megatron_lora.py: def lora_sha256(state): from rl_engine.models.muse_glimmer.e2e.sync import lora_sha256 as canonical; return canonical(state)  (import_lora then verifies with the same schema)

integration_findings.what: StrictTrainer(strict=False) has no LoRA: step() raises 'step requires strict=True', export_lora() calls export_binding_lora(None) -> AttributeError.
integration_findings.evidence: code reading of runtime/strict_trainer.py at 307fcf2 (not run)
integration_findings.patch: native trainer needs Bridge-native forward + the same LoRA wrapper with gradients (or the RFC drops the native-train modes)

integration_findings.what: StrictRolloutEngine(strict=False).load_lora raises 'load_lora is only available on a strict engine'; the loop syncs LoRA before rollout 0 in every mode.
integration_findings.evidence: code reading of runtime/strict_rollout_engine.py at 307fcf2 (not run)
integration_findings.patch: native rollout needs vLLM LoRA (enable_lora + LoRARequest from the exported tensors) or the strict LoRA slots on the native model

integration_findings.severity: weakens weight_sync_identity on the vLLM side (no hard failure)
integration_findings.what: StrictRolloutEngine.provenance() has no top-level lora_sha256 (only workers[i].lora_sha256), and worker_load_lora stores the DECLARED hash without recomputing it on the received tensors.
integration_findings.evidence: code reading; e2e/sync.rollout_lora_sha256 now accepts the per-worker hash when all TP workers agree (tested)
integration_findings.patch: load_lora: verify sync.lora_sha256(cpu_state) == sha256 before the RPC and recompute in worker_load_lora; expose provenance()['lora_sha256']

integration_findings.severity: risk for train TP2 when one rollout step takes > 10 min
integration_findings.what: strict_trainer._init_distributed uses the default NCCL timeout (10 min); the TP worker idles in broadcast_object_list while the orchestrator generates, so a long rollout (or vLLM start-up after the trainer is built) can trip the NCCL watchdog.

today's StrictTrainer spawns its own TP workers, so it must run under --trainer-launcher process; under torchrun the server passes gpu_ids=[LOCAL_RANK] and StrictTrainer fails closed on its len(gpu_ids)==tp check (no double spawn).
integration_findings.evidence: torchrun path tested with the mock trainer (TP2, gloo): all ranks run the same ops, rank LoRA hashes agree
integration_findings.patch: to use torchrun: StrictTrainer must build one rank per process when torch.distributed is already initialized

incident.what: CPU-only runs before 0738241 (tests and the first bench runs, no lease) created a CUDA context on GPU 0 for their duration: torch 2.13 Adam.step probes torch.accelerator.current_stream() even for CPU parameters. Fixed in mocks.CPUSafeAdam; test_cpu_mock_trainer_never_initializes_cuda guards it. Any CPU test that steps a torch.optim optimizer in a GPU-visible process has the same effect.
